author: Bowang
title: Reject non-ASCII digits in JsonTreeReader.nextInt/nextLong (#3063)
description:
* Reject non-ASCII digits in JsonTreeReader.nextInt/nextLong

The streaming JsonReader.nextInt() and nextLong() reject non-ASCII digit
variants (e.g. full-width U+FF10-FF19) since #2995, but JsonTreeReader
(the tree-based counterpart used by fromJson(JsonElement, ...)) still
silently coerces them via Integer.parseInt/Long.parseLong, which accept
any Unicode decimal digit. Add the same validateAscii check on the
string-token path so both readers behave consistently.

Fixes the tree-based counterpart of #2994.

* Apply spotless formatting to new tests

* Extract isAllAscii to reduce duplication with JsonReader

---------

Co-authored-by: Éamonn McManus <emcmanus@google.com>
summary: JsonTreeReader accepted non-ASCII Unicode digits for integers and longs instead of rejecting them like JsonReader does.

author: anish
title: Fix URI type adapter to preserve identity for non-ASCII URIs (#3067)
description:
* Fix URI type adapter to preserve identity for non-ASCII URIs

The URI type adapter was calling `URI.toASCIIString()` in its `write()` method, which percent-encodes non-ASCII characters and applies Unicode normalization. The `read()` method does not reverse this percent-encoding, causing URIs with international characters to lose their original identity during round-trip serialization. For example, `s3://bucket/path/Kankyō.png` would fail an equality check after being serialized and deserialized.

Signed-off-by: anish <anishesg@users.noreply.github.com>

* address review feedback: use toString() for consistency in testUriDeserialization

Signed-off-by: anish <anishesg@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: anish <anishesg@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Éamonn McManus <emcmanus@google.com>
summary: The URI adapter percent-encoded non-ASCII characters on serialization without decoding on read, corrupting international URIs.

author: Oleg Golberg
title: Fix: peekNumber rejects some numerals like 2^64 + "0" (#3034)
description:
* Fix: peekNumber rejects some numerals like 2^64 + "0"

Issue: the "leading zero" logic in peekNumber, which tries to reject octal representations,
does not account for long overflows. This results in valid numeric literals
like "184467440737095516160" (2^64 + "0") being rejected in STRICT parsing mode.

The easiest way to reproduce this is to serialize and deserialize a BigInteger with the
value above.

This is a minimal fix which adds an overflow check to the leading zero condition.

* strict
summary: JsonReader rejected valid large numeric literals in strict mode due to long overflow in the leading-zero check.

author: Adil Burak Şen
title: fix(proto): cap bitFieldXXX_ index to prevent OOM in LegacyProtoTypeAdapterFactory (#3027)
description:
* fix(proto): cap bitFieldXXX_ index to prevent OOM in LegacyProtoTypeAdapterFactory

LegacyProtoTypeAdapterFactory.buildPresenceMaskFromBitFields() reads
bitField<N>_ fields from the JSON stream. If an attacker-supplied JSON
contains an extremely large index (e.g. bitField67108863_), calling
BigInteger.shiftLeft(N * 32) allocates N/8 bytes of heap, making it
trivial to OOM the JVM from a small input.

Fix: compute maxGroupIndex = ceil(fieldWithPresenceToBitIndex.size() / 32)
and skip any bitField group whose index exceeds that bound, since groups
beyond that range cannot affect any presence bit checked by the adapter.

Adds a regression test that verifies a crafted oversized index is silently
ignored while valid fields in the same message are still deserialized.

* fix: add try-catch for NumberFormatException in bitField parsing

The BIT_FIELD_PATTERN regex already restricts the captured group to
\d{1,9} (1-9 decimal digits), which guarantees Integer.parseInt succeeds.
Adding an explicit try-catch satisfies static-analysis tools (CodeQL)
that cannot infer the regex-based invariant.

* fix(proto): simplify OOM fix — tighten BIT_FIELD_PATTERN to \d{1,4}

Replace the dynamic maxGroupIndex guard with the simpler regex approach
suggested in review: limit the captured index to 4 digits (max 9999).
Any real proto message has far fewer than 9999 bitField groups, so the
narrower pattern is a clean fix without added runtime logic.

Also update the test comment to reflect the new mechanism.
summary: Uncapped bitField indices in LegacyProtoTypeAdapterFactory allowed untrusted JSON to allocate excessive heap and cause an OutOfMemoryError.

author: Andrew Stellman
title: Fix duplicate key detection when first value is null (#3006)
description:
* Fix duplicate key detection when first value is null

MapTypeAdapterFactory detected duplicate map keys by checking the
return value of Map.put(): `if (replaced != null)`. This missed
duplicates where the first value was null, because Map.put() returns
null (the previous value) which passed the != null check.

For example, {"a":null,"a":1} was silently accepted as {a=1} instead
of throwing JsonSyntaxException("duplicate key: a").

Fix: check Map.containsKey() before put() instead of relying on the
return value of put(). This correctly detects duplicates regardless
of whether the first value is null.

Fixes both the object form and the array-of-entries form
(enableComplexMapKeySerialization).

* Apply spotless formatting
summary: Duplicate map keys were not detected when the previous value was null because Map.put returns null in that case.

author: Marcono1234
title: Fix missing bounds checks for JsonTreeReader.getPath() (#2001)
description:
There are situations where the stack of JsonTreeReader contains a JsonArray
or JsonObject without a subsequent Iterator, for example after calling peek()
or nextName().
When JsonTreeReader.getPath() is called afterwards it therefore must not
assume that a JsonArray or JsonObject is always followed by an Iterator.

The only reason why this never caused an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in
the past is because the stack has an even default size (32) so it would just
have read the next `null`.
However, if the stack had for example the default size 31, a user created a
JsonTreeReader for 16 JSON arrays nested inside each other, then called 15
times beginArray(), followed by peek() and getPath() the exception would
occur.
summary: Fixes potential `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` crashes in `JsonTreeReader.getPath()` when handling arrays or objects on the stack without following iterators.

summary: Prevents standard Java deserialization of internal classes to protect against potential denial-of-service attacks.

author: Marcono1234
title: Fix LongSerializationPolicy null handling being inconsistent with Gson (#1990)

Gson does not actually use the specified LongSerializationPolicy but instead
uses type adapters which emulate the behavior. However, previously Gson's
implementation did not match LongSerializationPolicy regarding null handling.

Because it is rather unlikely that LongSerializationPolicy has been used on
its own, this commit adjusts its implementation to match Gson's behavior
(instead of the other way around).
summary: Fixes `LongSerializationPolicy` to properly handle null values consistently with Gson's type adapter behavior.

summary: Prevents JsonReader from entering an invalid state when nextInt(), nextDouble(), or nextLong() fails during parsing.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: When EOF is encountered prematurely, Streams.parse() (and JsonParser) now throw JsonSyntaxException.
summary: Ensures Streams.parse() and JsonParser throw a JsonSyntaxException when encountering premature EOF instead of an incorrect exception or behavior.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Fixed issue 443 by relying on Streams.parse() to return a JsonNull on empty documents and throw a JsonParseException otherwise.
summary: Fixes handling of empty documents to return JsonNull and properly throw JsonParseException on invalid inputs.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Fix testStringEndingInSlash by fixing nextNonWhitespace to always return the character at buffer[pos-1].
summary: Fixes nextNonWhitespace in JsonReader to always return the character at buffer[pos-1], fixing strings ending in a slash.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Permit multiple top-level values in JsonWriter in lenient mode. Also fix some cases where we don't throw the right thing on a closed JsonWriter.
description:
I'd prefer to not support multiple top-level values, but we support it in JsonReader and it's easier to be consistent. Kevin Hayen's patch pointed me in the right direction here, but I needed to do more work to cover some of the edge cases.

Fixes issue 397.
summary: Permits multiple top-level values in JsonWriter in lenient mode and ensures correct exceptions are thrown when writing to a closed writer.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Write some tests prescribed by missing code coverage. I found a bug where our nonexecute prefix code causes a problem.
summary: Fixes an issue in JsonReader where handling the non-execute prefix caused improper parsing.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Fix tests broken by r1078.
summary: Fix broken type adapter behavior in TypeAdapters introduced by a previous commit.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Fix nullSafe() to not infinitely recurse on non-null input.
summary: Fix nullSafe() adapter to delegate to the wrapped adapter instead of recursively calling itself on non-null values.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Fix broken test in registering competing type hierarchy adapters.
description: I actually tried to replicate this test but got an error "type adapters conflict" when I was doing it. I suspect the problem was that I was trying to use 'Object' as the base of my type hierarchy and that class is somehow special.
summary: Fix an improper conflict error in GsonBuilder when registering competing type hierarchy adapters.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Fix type adapter precedence so that last-registered wins (except for tree type hierarchy adapters, which were always last).
summary: Fixes type adapter precedence so that the most recently registered adapter takes priority as expected.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Fix a regression I introduced with the changes to type hierarchy registration. If the registered type was a raw type, we need to also match the parameterizations of that type.
summary: Fixes a regression where registered type adapters for raw types failed to match parameterized variations of those types.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Throw JsonParseException in event of binding failures like type mismatches.
summary: Wraps binding failures and type mismatch exceptions into JsonParseException per the expected API contract.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Fix date adapters to work when run in any time zone.
summary: Date type adapters produced incorrect results or failed when executed in non-default time zones.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Implemented runtime type serialization for keys and values of a map. This fixes MoreSpecificTypeSerializationTest.testMapOfSubclassFields
summary: Map keys and values of subtype instances were serialized using declared types instead of runtime types.

author: Joel Leitch
title: A few minor fixes and one incompatible Java 1.6 API call.
summary: Replaces a Java 1.6-only API call that caused runtime errors on Java 1.5 environments.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: If the reflective type isn't as expected, fail with a JsonSyntaxException
summary: Throws JsonSyntaxException instead of an unexpected runtime exception when JSON does not match the reflective type.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Throw the right exceptions when primitives fail to parse.
summary: Fixes primitive type adapters to throw JsonSyntaxException instead of NumberFormatException when parsing invalid values.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Restored this behavior: If a type adapter is registered for a base class, then a field of that type is serialized with the type adapter instead of using the run-time type. This fixes: CustomSerializerTest.testBaseClassSerializerInvokedForBaseClassFieldsHoldingSubClassInstances
summary: Restores serialization behavior so that fields declared as a base class use the registered base class adapter instead of the runtime subtype adapter.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Fix a pair of relatively benign off-by-one bugs. These only manifest if the source Reader returns characters one-at-a-time.
summary: Fixes off-by-one errors in JsonReader when reading from a Reader that yields characters one at a time.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Fix integration tests that fell out from some benchmarking.
summary: Fixes issues in MiniGson and ReflectiveTypeAdapter that were causing integration test failures discovered during benchmarking.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Fix serialization where one type depends (possibly indireclty) on itself!
summary: Fixes an infinite recursion crash during serialization of recursive or self-referential types.

author: Joel Leitch
title: Quick fix for threading issue. Should maybe look into synchronizing this method instead.
summary: Fixes a thread-safety issue in FieldAttributes.

author: Joel Leitch
title: Fix a bunch of preserve-type issues: - Issue 205 - Issue 294 - Issue 318
summary: Fixes multiple issues where type preservation was not maintained during serialization.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Fixed the bug where copyOf() for a ParameterizedTypeHandlerMap was failing when hierarchical type adapters for a sub class and its base class were present.
description: Fixed previously broken tests to verify the behavior that a hierarchical type adapter for a sub-class can be registered after registering a hierarchical type adapter for the base-class. The vice-versa is not allowed as it would result in hiding the sub-class hierarchical type adapter.
summary: Fixes a failure in ParameterizedTypeHandlerMap.copyOf() when hierarchical adapters for subclasses and base classes are present.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Fix unsafe allocations on Android
summary: Fixes unsafe object allocation failure and crashes on Android platforms.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Revised CallPath to handle null or empty paths correctly. Updated ResourceQuery callspec to accept a list in the response body.
summary: Handles null or empty paths properly in CallPath.

author: Joel Leitch
title: Fixing parsing of unquoted strings to be (somewhat) consistent with previous versions of Gson. The difference with this version is that Gson will throw a more specific exception rather than JsonParseException.
summary: Fixes unquoted string parsing behavior to throw specific exceptions consistently with prior versions.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Don't return null on an unexpected EOF unless the document is empty. This brings us back to compatibility with GSON 1.5.
summary: Prevents returning null on unexpected EOF in Streams unless the document is empty.

author: Joel Leitch
title: Fix for Issue #40.
summary: Fixes an issue in TypeInfoFactory where generic type information was improperly resolved.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Fix a regression that expects different type adapters for long.class and Long.class. This is a temporary fix; later we may want to always use the canonical wrapped class.
summary: Fixes a regression where different type adapters were expected for primitive long and Long wrapper classes.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Fix primitive wrapping and casting.
description: Issue: 235
summary: Fixes primitive type wrapping and casting errors during deserialization.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: removed redundant null checks. Fixed bug in Streams.copy where it was not honoring the closeInput and closeOutput parameters. Suppressed spurious unused warnings
summary: Fixes Streams.copy failing to honor closeInput and closeOutput flags.

author: Jesse Wilson
title: Don't exclude enum constants, even if they are anonymous. See issue 226.
summary: Prevents anonymous enum constant classes from being incorrectly excluded from serialization.

author: Joel Leitch
title: Fix for Issue 178.
summary: Fixes Issue 178 regarding handling of null or empty JSON members in formatters.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Added checks to ensure that typeHierarchyAdapter being registered doesn't hide a previously existing one. Fixed a bug where registerIfAbsent was adding type adapters in the reverse order of priority. Added toString() to Pair.
summary: Fixes registerIfAbsent inserting type adapters in reverse priority order.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Added setting of content-length in requests even if the body is non existent. Fixed logs for requests. Ensured that streams are not inadvertently closed while copying output.
summary: Ensures streams are not inadvertently closed prematurely while copying output.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Fixed serializers and deserializers for java.sql Date and Time to ensure that Date does't serialize time, and time does't serialize the date portion.
summary: Fixes java.sql Date and Time serializers to exclude time from Date and date from Time in their outputs.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Ensured that custom deserializer is invoked with actual type returned for field values. Fixed a bug where a top-level object was constructed with default values even when the custom deserializer tried to set it to null.
summary: Ensures custom deserializers receive the actual field type and fixes top-level objects improperly defaulting when deserializers return null.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Fixed custom serilization invocation to correctly handle nulls returned by custom serializer.
summary: Corrects serialization handling when a custom serializer returns null.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Ensured that a custom handler is not visited during deserialization. Ensured that JsonTreeNavigator can handle null values as children of JsonObject. This is now possible since Gson exposes toJson(JsonElement) method to which the user can pass a JsonElement with null values.
summary: Prevents visiting custom handlers during deserialization and allows JsonTreeNavigator to navigate null values inside JsonObject.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Fixed Issue 153 by using a stack to keep track of first elements at any level.
summary: Tracks first elements per nesting level using a stack to fix incorrect JSON formatting in JsonPrintFormatter.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Fixed issue 162 by making default date adapter thread-safe by synchronizing serialize() and deserialize() methods.
summary: Synchronizes serialize and deserialize methods in the default date adapter to fix thread-safety issues with SimpleDateFormat.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Fixed issue 147. Integral values (byte, short, integer, long, BigInteger) are now comparable to each other. Floating point values (float, double, BigDecimal) are now comparable to each other.
summary: Enables proper comparison and equality checking between different integral and floating-point JsonPrimitive types.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Fixed bug 158
summary: Fixes bug 158 where Gson failed when attempting to serialize or deserialize certain types.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Fixed issue 126 by ensuring that parameterized type deduction is not done for transient fields.
summary: Skips type deduction on transient fields to prevent unnecessary type resolution failures and crashes.

author: Joel Leitch
title: Do not leak out a ClassCastException to our clients.
summary: Catches ClassCastException when casting elements and converts it to a standard JsonParseException.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Fixed the test that broke while fixing issue 100 in r394 by using a TreeSet for SortedSets and HashSet for other kind of sets.
summary: Uses TreeSet for SortedSet and HashSet for standard sets during deserialization to fix broken set instantiation.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Fixed issue 100 by adding support for deserialization of collections of elements that do not implement Comparable.
summary: Fixes collection deserialization failing with ClassCastException when element types do not implement Comparable.

author: Joel Leitch
title: Minor fixes for pretty printing.
summary: Fixes formatting defects in JsonPrintFormatter that caused incorrect pretty-printed output.

author: Joel Leitch
title: Wrapping UUID deserializer in exception wrapper to make it consistent with other deserializers
summary: Wraps the UUID deserializer in an exception wrapper so invalid UUID strings throw JsonParseException instead of an unhandled IllegalArgumentException.

author: Joel Leitch
title: Removal of all unnecessary "Default" InstanceCreators.  While refactoring the code, I found a bug that these InstanceCreators were being called when inside an "Array".  This bug is fixed in this change.
summary: Fixes a bug where default instance creators were erroneously invoked for elements nested inside arrays.

author: Joel Leitch
title: Fix parsing of double and big decimals that have an exponent but no fraction part.
summary: Fixes a parser error where numbers in scientific notation having an exponent without a fractional part failed to parse.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Fixed issue 66 to allow escaped slash ( \/) as a valid Json escaped character. Changed Gson version to 1.2.3.
summary: Fixes a parser failure that improperly rejected valid escaped forward slashes in JSON strings.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Fixed issue 63 where Gson could not operate in a thread-safe manner. Resolved the issue by recreating ObjectNavigatorFactory for each call instead of reusing the same object everywhere. This is needed since ObjectNavigatorFactory had MemoryRefStack that was incorrectly being shared across calls.
summary: Fixes thread-safety issues by avoiding the reuse of a shared MemoryRefStack instance across concurrent Gson calls.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Fixed issue 58 by disabling the use of field value actual type for all cases except when it is marked as Object.
summary: Fixes incorrect serialization of polymorphic fields by using declared types rather than runtime types unless the field is declared as Object.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: Fixed issue 53 where default date instances were not getting serialized/deserialized properly. Added support for time style as well by using he default formatter that uses time style.
summary: Fixes date serialization and deserialization errors by incorporating a default formatter that handles time styles.

author: Inderjeet Singh
title: fix for bug 56 where Gson wasn't serialization null fields of type string, collection and arrays properly even when serializeNulls was set.
summary: Fixes an issue where null fields of type String, Collection, and Array were omitted during serialization despite serializeNulls being enabled.

author: Joel Leitch
title: Fix pretty printing of interlacing arrays and objects.
summary: Fixes broken indentation and formatting when pretty printing interlacing JSON arrays and objects.
